title: Touching intervals
options: Yes — 3 <= 3, they share the point 3 and merge to [1, 5]
explanation: With <= the shared endpoint counts as overlap (LeetCode's Merge Intervals wants this). Meeting-room problems sometimes want strict < — read the problem's definition every time.

title: Drill: can attend all meetings?
prompt: From memory: given meeting intervals, return whether one person can attend them all (no two overlap; touching endpoints like [1,3],[3,5] are OK). Sort by start, then check each consecutive pair.

solution.explanation: After sorting, only NEIGHBORS can conflict — that's the entire power of sort-then-sweep. (This is LeetCode's Meeting Rooms.)

hints: Conflict: this meeting starts before the previous one ends — strict `<` here since touching is allowed.

title: Drill: count merged intervals
prompt: From memory (sort then sweep): return how many intervals remain after merging all overlaps. Sort by start, then sweep tracking the current merged end.
hints: Sort by start. A new merged interval begins when the next start is beyond the current end.
Otherwise extend the end with max.
